name: Marigold V2
plain: Relative depth from one photo by a very large image-generation model run for a single step: accurate but slow and memory-hungry (about 2 GB of GPU memory, 9 GB of host RAM).
summary: Marigold V2 (Pavlovic, Wandel, Obukhov et al. 2026): affine-invariant log depth by one rectified-flow step of Qwen-Image-Edit-2509's 20 B transformer (NF4 4-bit, as the authors run it) with a rank-128 depth LoRA and a fine-tuned Qwen VAE decoder (depth/Log-stage2).

papers.title: Marigold V2: Revisiting Diffusion Transformers for Monocular Depth Estimation

licence_notes: The converted weight file (NF4 transformer, LoRA, folded constants, 2-D VAE) is hosted by fastforks under the originals' Apache-2.0 licence; NOTICE keeps both attributions and lists the changes.
limitations: 20 B transformer in 4 bit: 8.4 GB of weights; by default (`stream=True`, CUDA) it runs in ~1-4 GB of device memory from 8.4 GB of page-locked host RAM (load fails with an error when less is free); `stream=False` keeps it resident (about 9-11 GB of device memory, 16 GB cards: up to ~1024 px).
Diffusion model: the VAE posterior sample comes from a CPU generator seeded with `seed` and differs from the original code's (unseeded, device) sample.
The enlargement to a multiple of 16 is bicubic (the original: OpenCV Lanczos); inputs with sides that are multiples of 16 are not resized.
The output is log depth up to scale and shift (`kind = "affine_invariant_log"`): align in log space, not with the other families' depth outputs.
A traced or exported module reuses the noise of its traced shape; CPU inference is possible but slow (bf16 GEMMs of a 20 B model).
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant`, `affine_invariant_log` (log depth) and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none. Normals-only models (`kind` `none`) return `result.normals` `[B, H, W, 3]` (unit vectors, camera frame: x right, y down, z forward).

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.02 vs the original. GPU, bfloat16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 1 % and p99 <= 5 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `depth`).
